text:
**My pick: the Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable Wireless Charging Stand with Qi2 25W ($129.99).**

Macworld's review calls it a strong desk pick. Here's what it offers:
- **iPhone:** up to 25W with Qi2.2.
- **Apple Watch:** a 5W module that Macworld says is enough for fast charging.
- **AirPods:** a 5W pad.
- **Stand:** the charging pad adjusts through a 160° viewing angle, and Macworld says no rival foldable stands as tall or adjusts as much.
- **In the box:** a 45W USB-C adapter with US, UK and EU plugs, plus a 4-ft cable.
- **Travel:** it folds to about 152 x 90 x 30mm and weighs 399g.
- **Downside:** it's larger and heavier than some smaller foldable chargers.

Where to buy it:
- [Satechi](https://satechi.com/products/3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-with-qi2-25w)
- [Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GNRSY36V)
- [Best Buy](https://www.bestbuy.com/product/satechi-3-in-1-qi2-25w-fast-wireless-charging-stand-magnetic-foldable-for-iphone-apple-watch-airpods-space-black/J3GWC4C8TW)
- [B&H](https://www.bhphotovideo.com/c/product/1960497-REG/satechi_st_q25f31c_ea_3_in_1_foldable_qi2_25w.html)
- [Walmart](https://www.walmart.com/ip/19875453032)

**Alternative: ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Qi2.2 25W ([buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand)).**
- It has a 25W magnetic phone pad, an Apple Watch pad, an earbuds pad, an active cooling fan and a 50W adapter.
- The list price is $99.99. The deals site says code PARTNER18 brings it to about $82, but that's the site's own claim, so check it at ESR's checkout.
- The link is an affiliate link that opens ESR's US store.
- Only some iPhones get the full 25W (iPhone 17 series, 16 Pro Max and 16 Plus on iOS 26). Other models get 20W or 15W.
- A 15W version costs $79.99.
- It comes with a 30-day return window and a 12-month warranty, which becomes 24 months if you register.
- I found no independent review of it, so its performance is unverified.

**Which to choose**
- Choose the Satechi if you want the best-reviewed option with the most adjustable stand, and it's also the one I could confirm with an independent review.
- Choose the ESR if you want to spend less and you have a recent iPhone that can use the 25W speed.

I couldn't open the WIRED roundup, so this comparison rests on the Macworld review and ESR's product page. I didn't read the other results.
